correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real a>b>0, nonnegativity on polygon edges forces p3=xy(A+Bx+Cy). Interpolation on top and slanted edges forces C=(a-b)B and fixes the affine denominator. Linear precision fixes the remaining three numerators. Their factorizations yield a necessary-and-sufficient two-half-space cone and strict positivity of q at all four polygon vertices. A polynomial cross-product separates parameter classes, and an explicit gcd argument rules out cancellation. SymPy independently verifies critical identities, reconstructs the general boundary solution and checks the known example. Finite rational grids are supplementary only.

originality.rationale: Primary full text arXiv:2611.02110v1 establishes underlying framework and one special cubic system, but not classification of all positive cubic/affine systems on trapezoids; a fully read published planar denominator theorem determines only minimum denominator degree. The theorem adds sharp entire projective interval, two extremal families, and necessity/sufficiency of positivity for all base ratios. Web, mathematical research record and local claim overlap searches revealed no dominating exact statement; priority remains historical-provisional.
residual_risks: A differently named older interpolation family might implicitly yield the same cone and positivity characterization; no exhaustive proof of historical uniqueness is claimed.
The Floater 2015 survey was verified through bibliographic abstract and cited background, not its complete copyrighted full text.
Extrapolations to numerators of degree at least four, non-affine denominators and higher polygons are outside scope.

value.rationale: This supplies a natural complete moduli and sharp positivity classification for the first non-simplicial polygon family in the intermediate-degree class highlighted by Baumbach–Winter Section 3.3. It distinguishes two extremal non-Wachspress systems, all their positive rational interpolants, and the unique quadratic member, rather than merely reproducing a known single example or textbook deduction. It has plausible use for selecting admissible low-degree geometric interpolation coordinates without claiming unproved performance.
